messages.content: At the start, Project Lumen aimed to build an offline medicine catalog for rural clinics with unreliable internet.
The first prototype used one large CSV. Staff could find medicines but could not trace each record to its source or date.
During the Pine Valley field trial, stale dosage records remained visible after an update, and staff could not tell which record was current.
The team replaced overwrite-in-place with append-only, source-linked versions and explicit current versus historical states.
Clinic devices have 2 GB RAM and 20 GB disk. The service must run locally with compact storage and should not call a model when no retrieval query is needed.
The pilot recovered 97% of requested facts across three clinic sessions. The team selected the versioned evidence catalog for the next trial and postponed automatic summaries.
The printed clinic manuals will use blue covers.

searches.query: Summarize Project Lumen from its original goal through the failed prototype, redesign, operating constraints, and pilot decision.
searches.reference: Project Lumen began as an offline rural-clinic medicine catalog. The single-CSV prototype lacked source and date traceability, and stale dosage records persisted after updates. The team shifted to append-only source-linked versions with current and historical states. Because clinic devices have 2 GB RAM and 20 GB disk and unreliable internet, it chose the compact local versioned evidence catalog for the next trial. The pilot recovered 97% of requested facts; automatic summaries were postponed.
